entry.title: Dissecting the GPU Load/Store Unit and Exposing Its Security Risks. GPUs are the main platform for large-scale machine learning and power the largest supercomputers.
entry.summary:
GPUs are the main platform for large-scale machine learning and power the largest supercomputers. Their load/store units (LSUs) often determine kernel performance and have been exploited in prior attacks. Yet what is known about the LSU is only a few isolated mechanisms and parameters, and even a single one has been enough for an attack.

entry.title: From Token Changes to Task Failures: Bit Flips in a Shared KV-Cache Block
entry.summary:
In LLM serving systems with prefix caching, each KV block of a shared system prompt is held in GPU memory as a single physical copy, which every request with that prompt reads. Our earlier work measured change and showed that one bit flip in such a block changes many later responses without making them visibly degenerate. This paper extends that work by measuring how often the changed responses are wrong.

entry.title: Package managers have an integrity problem
entry.summary:
I tested 25 of the most popular package managers to check whether they detect a compromised package repository injecting malicious code into legitimate packages. This code integrity problem could be solved using cryptographic hashes or signatures, but many package managers are still vulnerable to this threat. Of the 25 package managers reviewed 1 , fewer than half used lockfiles that checked for tampering by default, and only two verified the integrity of every package they downloaded.

Source: Trail of Bits Security Research · Tags: #infosec #cryptography #rust #databases

entry.title: G+G: A Fiat-Shamir Lattice Signature Based on Convolved Gaussians
entry.summary:
We describe an adaptation of Schnorr's signature to the lattice setting, which relies on Gaussian convolution rather than flooding or rejection sampling as previous approaches. It does not involve any abort, can be proved secure in the ROM and QROM using existing analyses of the Fiat-Shamir transform, and enjoys smaller signature sizes (both asymptotically and for concrete security levels).

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #post-quantum

entry.title: Correcting the modulus switch error in TFHE bootstrapping for real-valued computation
entry.summary:
Torus Fully Homomorphic Encryption (TFHE) enables the homomorphic evaluation of arbitrary functions via Programmable Bootstrapping (PBS). However, the modulus switching step inherent to bootstrapping introduces a rounding error that forces the discretization of the input space, limiting the achievable precision on real-valued inputs. We propose a correction algorithm based on a first-order Taylor expansion, applied after bootstrapping, that directly mitigates this rounding error.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: STIP: Efficient and Secure Non-Interactive Transformer Inference via Compact Packing
entry.summary:
Secure Transformer Inference (STFI) for LLMs aims to protect user inputs and model parameters. Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) enables non-interactive STFI without intermediate communication, but its computational overhead remains substantial. Advancements have accelerated inference by optimizing packing strategies and reducing rotations.

entry.title: Prop RFQ: Proprietary Request for Quote as Pressure-Aware Exit Pricing for Redeemable Real-World Asset Tokens
entry.summary:
Redeemable real-world asset tokens can trade onchain faster than their backing assets can be sold or settled. An immediate-exit facility must therefore distinguish the token’s reported net asset value (NAV) from the reserve available to pay sellers. Charging larger exits more can preserve that reserve, but a holder may avoid part of the charge by splitting the sale.

entry.title: Revisiting the Security of OleF, t-OleF, and OlÆF. We revisit the security of OleF, t-OleF, and OlÆF and identify two independent security flaws.
entry.summary:
We revisit the security of OleF, t-OleF, and OlÆF and identify two independent security flaws. First, we establish a mask-compensation relation between continuation and termination processing in OleF and t-OleF. Exploiting this relation, we construct a two-encryption-query distinguisher against OleF with advantage $1 − 2^{−2n}$ .

entry.title: Impossible Polytopic Cryptanalysis Extended: Attention to Block Ciphers with Oversized Keys
entry.summary:
Block ciphers whose key size exceeds their block size, such as the 192- and 256-bit variants of \textsf{AES}, the tweakable block ciphers \textsf{Deoxys-BC-256} and \textsf{Deoxys-BC-384} (standardized by ISO/IEC as \textsf{Deoxys-TBC}), and \textsf{ChiLow-32} (EUROCRYPT 2025), achieve a security level beyond the block size and are becoming increasingly prevalent. This paper extends the impossible polytopic attack (\ipa{}, proposed by Tyge Tiessen at EUROCRYPT 2016) and shows that it yields longer-round distinguishers, enables key recovery on more rounds, and extends to the known-plaintext (KP) setting. To this end, we formalize the bound-estimation-based \ipd{} underlying Tiessen's original work and establish a general framework for distinguisher construction, within which we develop two strategies---the large-Sbox strategy and the subtlety-aware strategy---that substantially reduce the construction cost.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp

entry.title: Universally Composable Almost-Everywhere Secure Computation
entry.summary:
Most existing work on secure multi-party computation (MPC) ignores a key idiosyncrasy of modern communication networks, that there are a limited number of communication paths between any two nodes, many of which might even be corrupted. The problem becomes particularly acute in the information-theoretic setting, where the lack of trusted setups (and the cryptographic primitives they enable) makes communication over sparse networks more challenging. The work by Garay and Ostrovsky [EUROCRYPT'08] on almost-everywhere MPC (AE-MPC), introduced ``best-possible security'' properties for MPC over such incomplete networks, where necessarily some of the honest parties may be excluded from the computation.

Source: IACR Cryptology ePrint Archive · Tags: #cryptography #zkp #rust #logic
